value: Study participants: 35 Swedish health care students (medical, nursing, dentistry)
Travel destinations: Indian peninsula (n=18) and Central Africa (n=17)
Fecal specimens collected at median 4 days before departure and 22 days after return
ESBL-producing E. coli acquisition: 12/18 (67%) from Indian peninsula, 0/17 from Central Africa
Exclusion criterion: no antibiotics within 6 months prior to sampling
Sequencing libraries: 70 total (before and after specimens from 35 individuals)
Range of read pairs per library: 57,708,298 to 463,791,736
Resistance genes detected: 178 different types across all specimens

extraction_warnings: Paper provides aggregate cohort-level data (n=35 total: 18 to India, 17 to Africa). Individual subject and sample identifiers are not disclosed, making sample-level extraction impossible. The schema requests sample_level granularity, but the paper does not publish per-participant data rows.
Sex/gender reported only as aggregate (74% female, 26/35); individual values cannot be extracted.
Age reported as range (23-34 years); individual ages per participant not provided.
Most biological and demographic fields are not reported at individual level; disease information (travelers' diarrhea) applies to ~69% of cohort but individual status not specified.
Study uses a paired before-and-after design rather than case-control, so 'control' classification is conceptually inappropriate but filled as 'Not Used' per schema requirements.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Schema contains many fields designed for cancer/clinical trial studies (RECIST, TNM staging, ECOG, tumor size); this paper is a microbiome/antibiotic resistance study of healthy travelers with no applicability to those fields.
Most schema fields are not relevant to this microbiome/resistance dissemination study. Only biomarker fields, feces_phenotype fields, and treatment fields yielded extracted values.
Granularity is study_level; paper reports aggregate statistics across 35 participants (17 to Africa, 18 to India) without per-sample data tables.

The schema includes fields designed for oncology/tumor studies (tumor_size_residual_measurement) which are not applicable to this microbiome/antibiotic resistance study.
